{"id":"persona-vvs2.8","title":"Signal handling: SIGTERM/SIGINT to a service control handler","description":"hired/src/main.rs:9 imports tokio::signal::unix and :52-53 install SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers for graceful shutdown. Neither exists on Windows.

Two cases and they are not the same:
  - run interactively: tokio::signal::ctrl_c covers it, a near-direct swap.
  - run as a service: Windows delivers stop requests through a SERVICE CONTROL
    HANDLER registered with the SCM, not as a signal. Ignoring that means the
    service cannot be stopped cleanly and the SCM kills it instead.

Which matters for the same reason as persona-vvs2.5: an unclean exit leaves the ephemeral signing key and pseudonym_ikm behind with no orderly handover, and consumers discover it as tokens signed by a kid the JWKS no longer carries.

{"description":"hired/src/main.rs:9 imports tokio::signal::unix and :52-53 install SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers for graceful shutdown. Neither exists on Windows.

Two cases and they are not the same:
  - run interactively: tokio::signal::ctrl_c covers it, a near-direct swap.
  - run as a service: Windows delivers stop requests through a SERVICE CONTROL
    HANDLER registered with the SCM, not as a signal. Ignoring that means the
    service cannot be stopped cleanly and the SCM kills it instead.

Which matters for the same reason as persona-vvs2.7: an unclean exit leaves the ephemeral signing key and pseudonym_ikm behind with no orderly handover, and consumers discover it as tokens signed by a kid the JWKS no longer carries.

Depends on the service lifecycle question in persona-vvs2.9 -- whether hired runs as a Windows service at all is that bead's decision, and this one is only interesting if the answer is yes."}
